summary.text: Lies and falsehoods personified, a plural brood that Eris (Strife) bore without a father among the dark powers that beset mortal life.
Hesiod names them in the catalogue of woes between Quarrels and Disputes, the spoken untruths that strife breeds in the human world.

story.text: In Hesiod's genealogy of woes, abhorred Eris (Strife) bore the Pseudea without union with any father, setting Lies among Toil, Forgetfulness, Famine, the tearful Sorrows, Battles, Murders and Oath — the dark powers that, born of discord, weave themselves into the texture of mortal existence.

Unlike most members of the catalogue the Pseudea are named in the plural, a swarming brood of falsehoods rather than a single figure. They stand between Quarrels and Disputes in the line that runs down to Oath, who most troubles men when one swears a false oath — placing spoken untruth at the heart of the discord that strife sows among mortals.

Hesiod gives the Pseudea no separate deed or myth. Like their siblings they are names made into forces: the lies and falsehoods that attend human dealings are given a place in the order of things, kin to the other afflictions of Night's wider household and answerable to the same moral economy that governs human suffering.
